paper_title: A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models
caption: The average performance of all models on Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness categories.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average performance of various language models across three categories: Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness. The vertical axis represents the performance score, ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis displays a list of language models, including Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407, Llama-3.1-Instruct, Llama-3.2-Instruct, Llama-3.2-70B-Instruct, Phi-3-medium-128k-instruct, Phi-3.5-mini-instruct, Llama-3.1-70B, ProLong-512k-instruct, Llama-3.1-88-instruct, glm-4-9b-chat-1m, gpt-40-mini-2024-04-14, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M, and intermlm3-8-instruct. Each model is represented by three bars, colored in blue, orange, and gray, corresponding to the Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness categories, respectively. The Understanding scores range from approximately 3.1 to 98.8, the Reasoning scores range from approximately 1.8 to 88.8, and the Trustworthiness scores range from approximately 4.4 to 91.7. The model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M has the tallest blue bar (98.8), while Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 has the shortest blue bar (3.1). The bars are not sorted; their order follows the list on the horizontal axis, with no bars visually emphasized beyond the color distinction representing each category.
